unit.sep: Construct directed turns and test invariants,centres and symmetry.
unit.careers: Illustrative mathematical pattern/design modelling;no real machinery or professional qualification.
unit.focus: Rotation properties,plane/Cartesian constructions,centre/angle recovery,plane/solid rotational symmetry and direct congruence.
unit.content: Properties of rotation; Rotation on different planes; Rotational symmetry; Rotation and Congruence
unit.phenomenon: A fictional pattern chart confuses a rotation with reflection and counts every cube axis as order4.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Fixed-pointer turns,nonorigin images,independent bisectors,identity limits,finite/continuous symmetry and labelled congruence.
unit.drivingQuestion: How is rotation applied in real-life situations?
unit.storylineThread: Properties→quarter turns→half/full turns→nonorigin centre→recover centre→identity limit→plane order→cube axes→other solids→congruence→use/digital evidence→independent final.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and Problem Solving: the learner draws objects and their images and through construction establishes the centres and angles of rotation.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner discusses using an object and its image on a plane surface to generate the properties of rotation.
unit.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of learning resources collected from the immediate environment to establish their axis and order of rotational symmetry.
Respect: learners appreciate each other’s opinion as they discuss and draw the image under a rotation given the object, centre and angle of rotation.
unit.pcis: Environmental education: as the learner responsibly collects regular solids from the immediate environment to determine the axis and order of rotational symmetry.

sections.title: 1. Construct and check a directed rotation
sections.prompt: Using CRT12,rotate the complete triangle90°clockwise about the origin on equal-unit axes. Label every image coordinate,centre and direction. Check each centre distance and explain one preserved angle/length property. Distinguish this construction from a reflection.
sections.exemplar: P′(0,−1),Q′(0,−3),R′(2,−1)by(x,y)→(y,−x). Centre distances1,3,√5are unchanged;corresponding angles and lengths are preserved. PQandPRare2unit perpendicular sides,as areP′Q′andP′R′. The fixed labelled orientation is preserved by the rotation;it is not a line reflection.

sections.title: 2. Determine centre and angle from images
sections.prompt: Use the separate CRT12 A/A′andB/B′pairs to construct perpendicular bisectors,determine the centre and state the directed angle modulo360°. Give both midpoint/bisector checks and verify the radius turn for both pairs. Explain why identity endpoints alone would not identify a unique centre.
sections.exemplar: AA′midpoint(2,1),bisectory=−x+3;BB′midpoint(2,2),bisectory=2;intersectionO(1,2). OApoints south andOA′east,90°counterclockwise;OBpoints southeast andOB′northeast,also90°counterclockwise. Identity endpoints permit any centre with0°orfull-turn multiples,so do not identify a unique centre.

sections.title: 3. Determine plane and solid symmetry
sections.prompt: For the CRT12 nonsquare rectangle,regular hexagon and circle,state the order and least positive matching angle where one exists. Describe a symmetry axis/order for the cube through opposite face centres,the triangular prism through base centres,and the right circular cone through apex/base centre. Distinguish finite order,continuous symmetry and the number of axis lines.
sections.exemplar: Rectangle2/180°;regularhexagon6/60°;circlecontinuous with no least positive matching angle. Cube opposite-face-centre axis order4;regulartriangularprism base-centre axis order3;rightcircularcone axial symmetry continuous. An axis is a line,its order counts matching turns about that line;these are not the same as counting how many axis lines a solid has.

sections.title: 4. Deduce congruence and explain a useful application
sections.prompt: Use your section1 triangle to justify congruence by a valid side/angle test and explain why the given rotation is direct congruence under the fixed labels. Write a specific correct application of rotation,with a checked example and a centre/angle/direction/idealisation limit. A reasoned method preference is accepted;do not claim an unobserved physical or digital action.
sections.exemplar: PQ=PR=2andincludedangleP90°;P′Q′=P′R′=2withincludedangle90°,soSASconfirmscongruence. Rotation preserves the fixed labelled orientation,so this is direct congruence. Accept a specific correct fixed-pointer,pattern or model application with numerical/geometric evidence and its condition;different-length clock hands are not automatically congruent images. Written evidence does not certify unobserved equipment/digital actions.
